solution: Alpha-hydrogens in ketones are acidic due to resonance stabilization of the conjugate base (enolate).
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: How many stereoisomers does the molecule $CH_3CH=CHCH_2CHBrCH_3$ have?
solution: One double bond (Geometrical Isomerism: 2) and one chiral carbon (Optical Isomerism: 2). Total stereoisomers = $2 \times 2 = 4$.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: The stability of carbanions in the following (a) $RC\equiv C^-$ (b) $R_2C=CH^-$ (c) $R_3C-CH_2^-$ is in the order of
solution: Stability depends on s-character of the carbon. $sp$ (50%) > $sp^2$ (33%) > $sp^3$ (25%). Order: a > b > c.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: The relative reactivities of acyl compounds towards nucleophilic substitution are in the order of
options: Acyl chloride > Ester > Acid anhydride > Amide
Acyl chloride > Acid anhydride > Ester > Amide
Ester > Acyl chloride > Amide > Acid anhydride
Acid anhydride > Amide > Ester > Acyl chloride
solution: Reactivity depends on the leaving group ability: $Cl^- > RCOO^- > RO^- > NH_2^-$. Order: Acyl chloride > Anhydride > Ester > Amide.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: Base strength of (a) $H_3CCH_2^-$ (b) $H_2C=CH^-$ (c) $H-C\equiv C^-$ is in the order of
solution: Basicity is inversely proportional to acidity / s-character. $sp^3 > sp^2 > sp$. Order: a > b > c.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: $H_3C-CH(CH_3)-CH=CH_2 + HBr \rightarrow A$. A (predominantly) is
solution: Electrophilic addition of $H^+$ forms a secondary carbocation. This undergoes 1,2-hydride shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation. Then $Br^-$ attacks. Product: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: In DNA, the complimentary bases are
options: Uracil and adenine; cytosine and guanine
Adenine and thymine; guanine and cytosine
Adenine and thymine; guanine and uracil
Adenine and guanine; thymine and cytosine
solution: In DNA, Adenine pairs with Thymine (A-T) and Guanine pairs with Cytosine (G-C).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one the following is most reactive towards electrophilic attack?
solution: Phenol has an -OH group which is strongly activating (+M effect), making the ring very reactive towards electrophiles. Chlorine is deactivating, Nitro is strongly deactivating. Benzyl alcohol has -OH not directly on the ring.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: An organic compound contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Its elemental analysis gave C, 38.71% and H, 9.67%. The empirical formula of the compound would be
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: In a $S_N2$ substitution reaction of the type $R-Br + Cl^- \xrightarrow{DMF} R-Cl + Br^-$, Which one of the following has the highest relative rate?
solution: $S_N2$ reaction is sensitive to steric hindrance. The least hindered alkyl halide reacts fastest. $CH_3CH_2Br$ is primary and least hindered among the options.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: Acetophenone when reacted with a base, $C_2H_5ONa$, yields a stable compound which has the structure?
solution: This is an Aldol condensation (Claisen-Schmidt type but self condensation of acetophenone). It forms dypnone ($Ph-C(CH_3)=CH-CO-Ph$).
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: In a reaction of aniline a coloured product C was obtained. $Aniline \xrightarrow{NaNO_2/HCl} A \xrightarrow{N,N-dimethylaniline} C$. The structure of C would be
solution: Aniline is diazotized to Benzene diazonium chloride. This couples with N,N-dimethylaniline at the para position to form p-dimethylaminoazobenzene (Butter Yellow dye).
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: Which of the following statements is not true?
options: Natural rubber is a 1, 4 - polymer of isoprene
In vulcanization, the formation of sulphur bridges between different chains make rubber harder and stronger
Natural rubber has the trans-configuration at every double bond
Buna-S is a copolymer of butadiene and styrene
solution: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene. Trans-1,4-polyisoprene is Gutta Percha.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: Which one of the following is an amine hormone?
solution: Thyroxine is an iodinated derivative of the amino acid tyrosine.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Select one of the following of important features distinguishing Gnetum from Cycas and Pinus and showing affinities with angiosperms
options: Absence of resin duct and leaf venation
Presence of vessel elements and absence of archegonia
solution: Gnetum belongs to the order Gnetales, which is considered the most advanced group of gymnosperms. It shares affinities with angiosperms due to the presence of vessels in the xylem and the absence of archegonia in the female gametophyte.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Thermococcus, Methanococcus and Methanobacterium exemplify
options: Bacteria that contain a cytoskeleton and ribosomes
Archaebacteria that contain protein homologous to eukaryotic core histones
Archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is negatively supercoiled
Bacteria whose DNA is relaxed or positively supercoiled but which have a cytoskeleton as well as mitochondria
solution: These organisms are Archaebacteria. While they are prokaryotic, some Archaea have histones (unlike Eubacteria), but the specific group mentioned (methanogens/thermophiles) often have distinct chromosomal packaging. The most accurate description among the choices provided in standard AIPMT contexts for this specific question is related to their DNA supercoiling and histone characteristics distinguishing them.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is heterosporous?
solution: Salvinia is a heterosporous pteridophyte, meaning it produces two kinds of spores (microspores and megaspores). Equisetum, Dryopteris, and Adiantum are homosporous.
subject: Biology

question_latex: In which one of the following male and female gametophytes do not have free living independent existence?
solution: Cedrus is a Gymnosperm. In gymnosperms (and angiosperms), the male and female gametophytes are highly reduced and dependent on the sporophyte; they do not have a free-living independent existence. Pteris (Pteridophyte) and Funaria/Polytrichum (Bryophytes) have independent gametophytes.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following groups of three animals each is correctly matched with their one characteristic morphological feature?
options: Liver fluke, Sea anemone, Sea cucumber - Bilateral symmetry
Centipede, Prawn, Sea urchin - Jointed appendages
Scorpion, Spider, Cockroach - Ventral solid central nervous system
solution: Scorpion, Spider, and Cockroach are all Arthropods. Non-chordates (like Arthropods) typically possess a ventral, solid, and double central nervous system. Taenia shows pseudometamerism. Sea anemone is radially symmetrical. Sea urchin (Echinoderm) has tube feet, not jointed appendages characteristic of arthropods.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following phyla is correctly matched with its two general characteristics?
options: Mollusca - Normally oviparous and development through a trochophore or veliger larva
Arthropoda - Body divided into head, thorax and abdomen and respiration by tracheae
Chordata - Notochord at some stage and separate anal and urinary openings to the outside
Echinodermata - Pentamerous radial symmetry and mostly internal fertilization
solution: Molluscs are generally oviparous and often have indirect development involving larvae like Trochophore or Veliger. Arthropods don't always have head/thorax/abdomen (e.g., cephalothorax in arachnids) and have diverse respiratory organs (gills, book lungs). Echinoderms mostly have external fertilization.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following in birds, indicates their reptilian ancestry?
options: Two special chambers crop and gizzard in their digestive tract
solution: The presence of epidermal scales on the hind limbs of birds is a distinct morphological feature inherited from reptilian ancestors.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Ascaris is characterized by
options: Presence of true coelom and metamerism
Absence of true coelom but presence of metamerism
Presence of neither true coelom nor metamerism
Presence of true coelom but absence of metamerism
solution: Ascaris (Aschelminthes) is a pseudocoelomate animal. It does not possess a true coelom (lined by mesoderm) and lacks metameric segmentation.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of phylum Annelida?
solution: Annelids possess a true coelom (eucoelom), not a pseudocoelom. Pseudocoelom is characteristic of Aschelminthes (Roundworms).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Cellulose is the major component of cell walls of
solution: Pythium is a member of Oomycetes (fungi-like protists), which typically have cell walls composed of cellulose. Saccharomyces (yeast) has chitin. Xanthomonas and Pseudomonas are bacteria with peptidoglycan walls.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Vacuole in a plant cell
options: Lacks membrane and contains water and excretory substances
Is membrane-bound and contains storage proteins and lipids
Is membrane-bound and contains water and excretory substances
solution: The plant vacuole is bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast and typically contains water, sap, excretory products, and other materials not useful for the cell.
subject: Biology

question_latex: A competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase is
solution: Malonate closely resembles succinate in structure and competitively inhibits the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase in the Krebs cycle.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Polysome is formed by
options: Ribosomes attached to each other in a linear arrangement
Several ribosomes attached to a single mRNA
Many ribosomes attached to a strand of endoplasmic reticulum
solution: A polysome (or polyribosome) is formed when multiple ribosomes attach to a single mRNA molecule to translate it simultaneously.
subject: Biology

question_latex:
Carbohydrates are commonly found as starch in plant storage organs. Which one of the following five properties of starch (a-e) make it useful as a storage material?
(a) Easily translocated
(b) Chemically non-reactive
(c) Easily digested by animals
(d) Osmotically inactive
(e) Synthesized during photosynthesis
The useful properties are
solution: Starch is suitable for storage because it is osmotically inactive (does not affect water potential) and chemically non-reactive (stable). Sugar is the translocatable form, not starch.
subject: Biology

question_latex: In the light of recent classification of living organisms into three domains of life (bacteria, archaea and eukarya), which one of the following statements is true about archaea?
options: Archaea resemble eukarya in all respects
Archaea have some novel features that are absent in other prokaryotes and eukaryotes
Archaea completely differ from both prokaryotes and eukaryotes
solution: Archaea are prokaryotes but differ from bacteria in cell wall structure (lack peptidoglycan) and membrane lipids (branched chains). They share some features with eukaryotes (like histone proteins associated with DNA) but possess unique features allowing them to live in extreme environments.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Keeping in view the 'fluid mosaic model' for the structure of cell membrane, which one of the following statements is correct w.r.t. the movement of lipids and proteins from one lipid monolayer to the other (described as flip-flop movement)?
options: Neither lipids nor proteins can flip-flop
Both lipids and proteins can flip-flop
While lipids can rarely flip-flop, proteins cannot
While proteins can flip-flop, lipids cannot
solution: Lipids can undergo flip-flop movement (transverse diffusion), though it is slower than lateral diffusion. Membrane proteins are generally too large and polar to flip-flop across the hydrophobic core of the bilayer.
subject: Biology

question_latex: In germinating seeds fatty acids are degraded exclusively in the
solution: In germinating oilseeds, fatty acids are converted to carbohydrates via the glyoxylate cycle, which takes place in specialized peroxisomes called glyoxysomes.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The two sub-units of ribosome remain united at a critical ion level of
solution: Magnesium ions ($Mg^{2+}$) are essential for the structural integrity of ribosomes and for binding the two subunits (large and small) together.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of cucurbita are example of
solution: Thorns of *Bougainvillea* and tendrils of *Cucurbita* are both modified stems (axillary buds), so they share the same origin and basic structure. They are homologous organs.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Haploids are more suitable for mutation studies than the diploids. This is because
options: All mutations, whether dominant or recessive are expressed in haploids
Haploids are reproductively more stable than diploids
Mutagens penetrate in haploids more effectively than diploids
Haploids are more abundant in nature than diploids
solution: In haploids, there is only one set of chromosomes. Therefore, every gene, whether dominant or recessive, is expressed immediately in the phenotype. There is no masking of recessive mutations by dominant alleles as in diploids.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following pairs of nitrogenous bases of nucleic acids, is wrongly matched with the category mentioned against it?
solution: Adenine is a Purine, but Thymine is a Pyrimidine. Therefore, the pair Adenine, Thymine is wrongly categorized as Purines.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following conditions in humans is correctly matched with its chromosomal abnormality/ linkage?
solution: Klinefelter's syndrome is characterized by the karyotype 47, XXY (44 Autosomes + XXY). Down syndrome is Trisomy 21. Color blindness is X-linked. Erythroblastosis foetalis relates to Rh incompatibility.
subject: Biology

question_latex: In the DNA molecules
options: There are two strands which run antiparallel-one in $5'\rightarrow3'$ direction and other in $3'\rightarrow5'$
The total amount of purine nucleotides and pyrimidine nucleotides is not always equal
There are two strands which run parallel in the $5'\rightarrow3'$ direction
The proportion of Adenine in relation to thymine varies with the organism
solution: DNA is a double helix where the two strands are antiparallel: one runs $5' \to 3'$ and the other $3' \to 5'$. Chargaff's rules state purines = pyrimidines and A = T.
subject: Biology

question_latex: What is true about the isolated small tribal populations?
options: There is no change in population size as they have a large gene pool
There is a decline in population as boys marry girls only from their own tribe
Hereditary diseases like colour blindness do not spread in the isolated population
Wrestlers who develop strong body muscles in their life time pass this character on to their progeny
solution: Isolated small populations practicing endogamy (marrying within the tribe) often suffer from inbreeding depression and a decline in population fitness/size over time. Genetic drift is also significant.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following scientist's name is correctly matched with the theory put forth by him?
options: Weismann - Theory of continuity of Germplasm
solution: August Weismann proposed the Theory of Continuity of Germplasm. Mendel is the father of genetics. Pasteur disproved spontaneous generation. de Vries proposed Mutation Theory.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is incorrect about the characteristics of protobionts (coacervates and microspheres) as envisaged in the abiogenic origin of life?
options: They could maintain an internal environment
They could separate combinations of molecules from the surroundings
They were partially isolated from the surroundings
solution: Protobionts (like coacervates and microspheres) exhibited some life-like properties (isolation, metabolism-like reactions) but they could not reproduce precisely. Reproduction is a defining characteristic of true living cells.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Darwin's Finches are an excellent example of
solution: Darwin's finches on the Galapagos Islands are a classic example of adaptive radiation, where a single ancestral species diversified into multiple species adapted to different ecological niches.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following pairs of items correctly belongs to the category of organs mentioned against it?
options: Wings of honey-bee and wings of crow - Homologous organs
Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita - Analogous organs
Nictitating membrane and blind spot in human eye - Vestigial organs
Nephridia of earthworm and malpighian tubules of cockroach - Excretory organs
solution: Nephridia (earthworm) and Malpighian tubules (cockroach) are both excretory organs. Wings of bee and crow are Analogous. Thorns and tendrils are Homologous. Blind spot is functional (exit of optic nerve), not vestigial.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The fruit is chambered, developed from inferior ovary and has seeds with succulent testa in
solution: Pomegranate (Balausta fruit) develops from a multilocular inferior ovary. The edible part is the succulent testa of the seeds.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The $C_4$ plants are photosynthetically more efficient than $C_3$ plants because
options: $CO_2$ generated during photorespiration is trapped and recycled through PEP carboxylase
solution: $C_4$ plants are more efficient because they lack photorespiration and often have a higher number of chloroplasts, particularly in the bundle sheath cells (Kranz anatomy). The primary reason is the absence of photorespiration due to the $C_4$ mechanism concentrating $CO_2$. Among the options, 'having more chloroplasts' is a feature contributing to efficiency, though the mechanism is key. Note: AIPMT key selected 1. However, the fundamental reason is minimized photorespiration. Option 3 implies photorespiration occurs but is recycled, which is technically incorrect ($C_4$ prevents it).
subject: Biology

question_latex: The chemiosmotic coupling hypothesis of oxidative phosphorylation proposes that adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is formed because
options: There is a change in the permeability of the inner mitochondrial membrane toward adenosine diphosphate (ADP)
High energy bonds are formed in mitochondrial proteins
ADP is pumped out of the matrix into the intermembrane space
A proton gradient forms across the inner membrane
solution: According to the chemiosmotic hypothesis, ATP synthesis is driven by the energy stored in a proton gradient generated across the inner mitochondrial membrane.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Dry indehiscent single-seeded fruit formed from bicarpellary syncarpous inferior ovary is
solution: Cypsela is a dry, indehiscent, single-seeded fruit that develops from a bicarpellary, syncarpous, inferior ovary (characteristic of Asteraceae).
subject: Biology

question_latex: The rupture and fractionation do not usually occur in the water column in vessel/tracheids during the ascent of sap because of
solution: The continuity of the water column is maintained by the high tensile strength of water resulting from Cohesion (between water molecules) and Adhesion (between water and walls).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Senescence as an active developmental cellular process in the growth and functioning of a flowering plant, is indicated in
solution: Leaf abscission is a regulated process involving senescence and the formation of an abscission layer, allowing the plant to shed organs.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Vascular tissues in flowering plants develop from
solution: According to the Histogen theory, Plerome gives rise to the central core (stele) which includes vascular tissues. Dermatogen -> Epidermis, Periblem -> Cortex.
subject: Biology

question_latex: In leaves of $C_4$ plants malic acid synthesis during $CO_2$ fixation occurs in
solution: In $C_4$ plants, initial $CO_2$ fixation by PEP carboxylase occurs in the Mesophyll cells, forming Oxaloacetic acid which is converted to Malic acid.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Importance of day length in flowering of plants was first shown in
solution: Photoperiodism was first discovered by Garner and Allard in the 'Maryland Mammoth' variety of Tobacco.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Endosperm is consumed by developing embryo in the seed of
solution: Pea is a non-endospermic (exalbuminous) seed where the endosperm is fully consumed by the developing embryo. Maize, Coconut, and Castor are endospermic seeds.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Nitrogen fixation in root nodules of Alnus is brought about by
solution: Frankia, an actinomycete, forms nitrogen-fixing root nodules in non-leguminous plants like Alnus.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The energy releasing process in which the substrate is oxidised without an external electron acceptor is called
solution: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of substrates where the organic molecule itself (or its derivative) acts as the final electron acceptor, without an external acceptor like Oxygen.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Replum is present in the ovary of flower of
solution: Replum is a false septum found in the ovary of members of the Brassicaceae family (e.g., Mustard), making the unilocular ovary bilocular.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The fleshy receptacle of syconus of fig encloses a number of
solution: Syconus fruit (Fig) develops from a hypanthodium inflorescence. The fleshy receptacle encloses many small achenes (fruitlets).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Electrons from excited chlorophyll molecule of photosystem II are accepted first by
solution: In PSII, the primary electron acceptor is Pheophytin, which passes the electron to Plastoquinone (a Quinone). Among the options, Quinone is the correct initial acceptor component.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which type of white blood cells are concerned with the release of histamine and the natural anticoagulant heparin?
solution: Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin, playing a key role in inflammatory reactions.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is the true description about an animal concerned?
options: Cockroach - 10 pairs of spiracles (2 pairs on thorax and 8 pairs on abdomen)
Earthworm - The alimentary canal consists of a sequence of pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, gizzard and intestine
Frog - Body divisible into three regions - head, neck and trunk
Rat - Left kidney is slightly higher in position than the right one
solution: Cockroach has 10 pairs of spiracles: 2 thoracic and 8 abdominal. In Earthworm, the sequence is Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Gizzard -> Stomach -> Intestine. Frog lacks a neck. In rats (and most mammals), the right kidney is often slightly lower due to the liver, but option A is factually the most standard correct description for Cockroach spiracles.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is the correct matching of the site of action on the given substrate, the enzyme acting upon it and the end product?
solution: Pancreatic $\alpha$-amylase acts on starch in the small intestine to produce disaccharides (Maltose). Pepsin acts in the stomach. Trypsin acts on proteins, not fats. Lipase produces fatty acids and glycerol, not micelles.
subject: Biology

question_latex: What is vital capacity of our lungs?
options: Total lungs capacity minus residual volume
Inspiratory reserve volume plus tidal volume
Total lungs capacity minus expiratory reserve volume
Inspiratory reserve volume plus expiratory reserve volume
solution: Vital Capacity (VC) = Total Lung Capacity (TLC) - Residual Volume (RV). It is also VC = TV + IRV + ERV.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is the correct difference between Rod Cells and Cone Cells of our retina?
options: Distribution: Rods - More concentrated in centre of retina; Cones - Evenly distributed all over retina
Visual acuity: Rods - High; Cones - Low
Visual pigment contained: Rods - Iodopsin; Cones - Rhodopsin
Overall function: Rods - Vision in poor light; Cones - Colour vision and detailed vision in bright light
solution: Rods are responsible for scotopic vision (dim light). Cones are responsible for photopic vision (bright light) and color vision. Rods contain Rhodopsin, Cones contain Iodopsin.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following items gives its correct total number?
solution: Humans have 2 pairs of floating ribs (11th and 12th), total = 4. Cervical vertebrae are 7. Amino acids in proteins are 20.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Given below is a diagrammatic cross section of a single loop of human cochlea. Which one of the following options correctly represents the names of three different parts?
question_svg: <svg width='200' height='150' viewBox='0 0 200 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='100' cy='75' r='60' fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M45,60 Q100,40 155,60' fill='none' stroke='black'/><path d='M45,90 Q100,110 155,90' fill='none' stroke='black'/><text x='100' y='35'>A</text><text x='100' y='75'>B</text><text x='100' y='125'>C</text></svg>
options: A: Perilymph, B: Tectorial membrane, C: Endolymph
B: Tectorial membrane, C: Perilymph, D: Secretory cells
C: Endolymph, D: Sensory hair cells, A: Serum
D: Sensory hair cells, A: Endolymph, B: Tectorial membrane
solution: In the cochlea cross-section: A is the Scala Vestibuli (contains Perilymph), Middle is Scala Media (contains Endolymph), C is Scala Tympani (contains Perilymph). The membrane shown (B) is the Tectorial membrane over the Organ of Corti. Option A (A: Perilymph, B: Tectorial Membrane, C: Endolymph) aligns best with standard diagrams where A is top, C is middle/bottom fluid spaces.
subject: Biology

question_latex:
Given below are four methods (A - D) and their modes of action (a - d) in achieving contraception. Select their correct matching from the four options that follow:

Method | Mode of Action
--- | ---
(A) The pill | (a) Prevents sperms reaching cervix
(B) Condom | (b) Prevents implantation
(C) Vasectomy | (c) Prevents ovulation
(D) Copper T | (d) Semen contains no sperms
solution: Oral contraceptive pills prevent ovulation. Condoms prevent sperms from reaching the cervix. Vasectomy ensures semen contains no sperms. Copper T (IUD) prevents implantation and fertilization.
subject: Biology

question_latex: What will happen if the secretion of parietal cells of gastric glands is blocked with an inhibitor?
options: Enterokinase will not be released from the duodenal mucosa and so trypsinogen is not converted to trypsin
Gastric juice will be deficient in chymosin
Gastric juice will be deficient in pepsinogen
In the absence of HCl secretion, inactive pepsinogen is not converted into the active enzyme pepsin
solution: Parietal cells secrete HCl and Intrinsic Factor. HCl is required to convert inactive pepsinogen into active pepsin. Without HCl, protein digestion in the stomach is impaired.
subject: Biology

question_latex: During the propagation of a nerve impulse, the action potential results from the movement of
options: $Na^+$ ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid
$K^+$ ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid
$Na^+$ ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid
$K^+$ ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid
solution: During depolarization (action potential generation), voltage-gated $Na^+$ channels open, causing a rapid influx of $Na^+$ ions from the extracellular fluid into the axoplasm (intracellular fluid).
subject: Biology

question_latex: The blood calcium level is lowered by the deficiency of
solution: Parathormone (PTH) increases blood calcium levels by stimulating bone resorption and reabsorption in kidneys. Its deficiency leads to lowered blood calcium (hypocalcemia). Calcitonin lowers blood calcium.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The most active phagocytic white blood cells are
solution: Neutrophils and Monocytes (which differentiate into macrophages) are the main phagocytic cells of the immune system responsible for engulfing pathogens.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Earthworms have no skeleton but during burrowing, the anterior end becomes turgid and acts as a hydraulic skeleton. It is due to
solution: The coelomic fluid in earthworms acts as a hydrostatic skeleton. Contraction of muscles against this incompressible fluid allows the worm to change shape and burrow.
subject: Biology

question_latex: In humans, blood passes from the post caval to the diastolic right atrium of heart due to
options: Pressure difference between the post caval and atrium
Pushing open of the venous valves
Stimulation of the sino auricular node
solution: Blood flows from veins (higher pressure relative to atrium during diastole) into the atrium (lower pressure). The pressure gradient drives the flow.
subject: Biology

question_latex: In humans, at the end of the first meiotic division, the male germ cells differentiate into the
solution: Primary spermatocytes undergo Meiosis I to form two haploid Secondary Spermatocytes.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is resistant to enzyme action?
solution: Pollen exine is made of sporopollenin, which is one of the most resistant organic materials known. It can withstand high temperatures, strong acids, and alkali, and no enzyme that degrades sporopollenin is known.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The length of different internodes in a culm of sugarcane is variable because of
options: Size of leaf lamina at the node below each internode
solution: Intercalary meristems are located at the base of internodes (in grasses like sugarcane) and are responsible for the elongation of internodes.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following pairs of plant structures has haploid number of chromosomes?
options: Megaspore mother cell and antipodal cells
solution: Egg cell (n) and Antipodal cells (n) are part of the female gametophyte (embryo sac) and are haploid. Secondary nucleus is diploid (2n), Nucellus is diploid (2n), MMC is diploid (2n).
subject: Biology

question_latex: What does the filiform apparatus do at the entrance into ovule?
options: It guides pollen tube from a synergid to egg
It helps in the entry of pollen tube into a synergid
It prevents entry of more than one pollen tube into the embryosac
It brings about opening of the pollen tube
solution: The filiform apparatus is present at the micropylar end of synergids. It releases chemicals that guide the pollen tube into the synergid.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Unisexuality of flowers prevents
solution: Unisexuality (Dicliny) prevents Autogamy (self-pollination within the same flower) but does not prevent Geitonogamy (pollination between different flowers of the same plant) if the plant is monoecious (bearing both male and female flowers).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which extraembryonic membrane in humans prevents desiccation of the embryo inside the uterus?
solution: The Amnion encloses the amniotic cavity filled with amniotic fluid, which protects the embryo from desiccation and mechanical shock.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about menstruation?
options: The beginning of the cycle of menstruation is called menarche
During normal menstruation about 40 ml blood is lost
The menstrual fluid can easily clot
At menopause in the female, there is especially abrupt increase in gonadotropic hormones
solution: Menstrual blood does not clot easily because of the presence of fibrinolysin (plasmin). It is usually in a liquid state.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The haemoglobin of a human foetus
options: Has a higher affinity for oxygen than that of an adult

question_latex: A slab consists of two layers of different materials of the same thickness and having thermal conductivities $K_1$ and $K_2$ are connected in series. The equivalent thermal conductivity of the slab is
solution:
For series combination of two slabs of equal thickness $d$: $R_{eq} = R_1 + R_2$. 
$\frac{2d}{K_{eq}A} = \frac{d}{K_1 A} + \frac{d}{K_2 A}$. 
$\frac{2}{K_{eq}} = \frac{1}{K_1} + \frac{1}{K_2}$. 
$K_{eq} = \frac{2K_1 K_2}{K_1 + K_2}$.

question_latex: A bulb and a condenser are connected in series with an A.C. source. On increasing the frequency of the source its brightness will

question_latex: What is the correct relationship between the pHs of isomolar solutions of sodium oxide ($pH_1$), sodium sulphide ($pH_2$), sodium selenide ($pH_3$) and sodium telluride ($pH_4$)?
solution:
These are salts of strong base (NaOH) and weak acids ($H_2O, H_2S, H_2Se, H_2Te$). The basicity of the anion depends on the strength of the conjugate acid. Acid strength: $H_2O < H_2S < H_2Se < H_2Te$. Weaker the acid, stronger the conjugate base. 
Basicity order: $O^{2-} > S^{2-} > Se^{2-} > Te^{2-}$. 
Therefore, pH order: $pH_1 > pH_2 > pH_3 > pH_4$.
subject: Chemistry

question_latex: The root mean square speed of the molecules of diatomic gas is u. When the temperature is doubled, the molecules dissociate into two atoms. The new rms speed of the atom is
solution:

New temp $T' = 2T$.

$u' = \sqrt{\frac{3R(2T)}{M/2}} = \sqrt{4 \frac{3RT}{M}} = 2u$.

question_latex: For the following concentration cell, to be spontaneous $Pt(H_2)P_1$ atm | $HCl$ | $Pt(H_2)P_2$ atm. Which of the following is correct?

Overall: $H_2(P_1) \rightarrow H_2(P_2)$. 
$E_{cell} = - \frac{RT}{nF} \ln(P_2/P_1) = \frac{RT}{nF} \ln(P_1/P_2)$. 
For spontaneity, $E > 0$, so $\ln(P_1/P_2) > 0 \implies P_1 > P_2$.

question_latex: The standard oxidation potential $E^{\circ}$ for the half cell reaction are $Zn \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + 2e^-; E^{\circ} = +0.76 V$ and $Fe \rightarrow Fe^{2+} + 2e^-; E^{\circ} = +0.41 V$. EMF of the cell reaction $Zn + Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + Fe$ is

question_latex: A unit cell of sodium chloride has four formula units. The edge length of the unit cell is 0.0564 nm. What is the density of sodium chloride?
solution:
Density $\rho = \frac{Z \cdot M}{N_A \cdot a^3}$. 
$Z = 4$, $M = 58.5$. $a = 0.0564$ nm = $5.64 \times 10^{-8}$ cm. 
$\rho = \frac{4 \times 58.5}{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times (5.64 \times 10^{-8})^3} \approx 2.16$ g/cm3.

question_latex: In the nuclear decay given below:\n$${}_{Z}X \longrightarrow {}_{Z+1}Y \longrightarrow {}_{Z-1}^{A-4}B^{*} \longrightarrow {}_{Z-1}^{A-4}B$$\nthe particles emitted in the sequence are:
solution:
The decay sequence is:
$${}_{Z}^{A}X \xrightarrow{ eta} {}_{Z+1}^{A}Y \xrightarrow{\alpha} {}_{Z-1}^{A-4}B^{*} \xrightarrow{\gamma} {}_{Z-1}^{A-4}B$$
1. ${}_{Z}X 	o {}_{Z+1}Y$: The atomic number increases by 1, mass number remains same. This is $ eta$-decay ($e^-$).
2. ${}_{Z+1}Y 	o {}_{Z-1}^{A-4}B^*$: The atomic number decreases by 2 ($Z+1 	o Z-1$) and mass number decreases by 4. This is $\alpha$-decay (${}_2^4	ext{He}$).
3. ${}_{Z-1}^{A-4}B^* 	o {}_{Z-1}^{A-4}B$: The nucleus goes from excited state to ground state. This is $\gamma$-decay.
Sequence: $ eta, \alpha, \gamma$.
subject: Physics

question_latex: A thin circular ring of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating in a horizontal plane about an axis vertical to its plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega$. If two objects each of mass $m$ be attached gently to the opposite ends of a diameter of the ring, the ring will then rotate with an angular velocity:
solution:
From conservation of angular momentum: $L_i = L_f$
$I_1 \omega_1 = I_2 \omega_2$
Initial moment of inertia $I_1 = MR^2$.
Final moment of inertia $I_2 = MR^2 + 2mR^2$ (two masses $m$ at distance $R$).
$MR^2 \omega = (MR^2 + 2mR^2) \omega_2$
$\omega_2 =  rac{MR^2}{R^2(M+2m)} \omega =  rac{M}{M+2m} \omega$.
subject: Physics

question_latex: A simple pendulum performs simple harmonic motion about $x=0$ with an amplitude $a$ and time period $T$. The speed of the pendulum at $x = \frac{a}{2}$ will be:
solution:
Velocity in SHM is given by $v = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - x^2}$.
Here $A = a$ and $x =  rac{a}{2}$.
$v = \omega \sqrt{a^2 -  rac{a^2}{4}} = \omega \sqrt{ rac{3a^2}{4}} = \omega  rac{a\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
Since $\omega =  rac{2\pi}{T}$,
$v =  rac{2\pi}{T} \cdot  rac{a\sqrt{3}}{2} =  rac{\pi a \sqrt{3}}{T}$.

question_latex: The two ends of a rod of length $L$ and a uniform cross-sectional area $A$ are kept at two temperatures $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$ $(T_{1} > T_{2})$. The rate of heat transfer, $\frac{dQ}{dt}$, through the rod in a steady state is given by:
solution: The rate of heat conduction is given by Fourier's law: $\frac{dQ}{dt} = kA \frac{\Delta T}{\Delta x}$.\nHere, $\Delta T = T_1 - T_2$ and $\Delta x = L$.\nSo, $\frac{dQ}{dt} = \frac{kA(T_{1}-T_{2})}{L}$.
subject: Physics

question_latex: A p-n photodiode is fabricated from a semiconductor with a band gap of 2.5 eV. It can detect a signal of wavelength:

$ rac{hc}{\lambda} \ge E_g \implies \lambda \le  rac{hc}{E_g}$
$\lambda_{max} =  rac{12400 	ext{ eV \AA}}{2.5 	ext{ eV}} = 4960 	ext{ \AA}$.
The wavelength must be less than 4960 \AA. Among the options, 4000 \AA is the only one satisfying this condition.

question_latex: A transistor is operated in common-emitter configuration at $V_{C} = 2$ V such that a change in the base current from 100 $\mu$A to 200 $\mu$A produces a change in the collector current from 5 mA to 10 mA. The current gain is:

question_latex: Four identical thin rods each of mass $M$ and length $l$, form a square frame. Moment of inertia of this frame about an axis through the centre of the square and perpendicular to its plane is:
solution:
Moment of inertia of one rod about an axis passing through its center and perpendicular to it is $I_{cm} =  rac{Ml^2}{12}$.

question_latex: A rectangular, a square, a circular and an elliptical loop, all in the $(x-y)$ plane, are moving out of a uniform magnetic field with a constant velocity, $\vec{V} = v\hat{i}$. The magnetic field is directed along the negative z axis direction. The induced emf, during the passage of these loops, out of the field region, will not remain constant for:
options: the circular and the elliptical loops.
the rectangular, circular and elliptical loops.
solution:
Induced emf $\varepsilon = Blv$. Here $l$ is the effective length of the conductor cutting the field lines.
For a rectangular or square loop moving along its side, the length $l$ inside the field remains constant until it fully exits. So emf is constant.
For circular and elliptical loops, the vertical length of the chord cutting the field boundary changes as the loop moves out. So emf varies.
Therefore, emf will not remain constant for the circular and elliptical loops.

question_latex: A galvanometer having a coil resistance of $60 \Omega$ shows full scale deflection when a current of 1.0 amp passes through it. It can be converted into an ammeter to read currents upto 5.0 amp by:
options: putting in series a resistance of $15 \Omega$
putting in series a resistance of $240 \Omega$
putting in parallel a resistance of $15 \Omega$
putting in parallel a resistance of $240 \Omega$
solution:
To convert a galvanometer to an ammeter, a shunt resistance $S$ is connected in parallel.
Formula: $I_g G = (I - I_g) S$
Given $G = 60 \Omega$, $I_g = 1.0$ A, $I = 5.0$ A.
$1.0 	imes 60 = (5.0 - 1.0) S$
$60 = 4 S \implies S = 15 \Omega$.
So, put $15 \Omega$ in parallel.

question_latex: Power dissipated in an LCR series circuit connected to an a.c source of emf $\epsilon$ is:
solution:
Power dissipated $P = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos\phi$.
$I_{rms} =  rac{\epsilon}{Z}$, $\cos\phi =  rac{R}{Z}$.
$P = \epsilon \cdot  rac{\epsilon}{Z} \cdot  rac{R}{Z} =  rac{\epsilon^2 R}{Z^2}$.
$Z^2 = R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2 = R^2 + (L\omega -  rac{1}{C\omega})^2$.
So, $P =  rac{\epsilon^2 R}{R^2 + (L\omega -  rac{1}{C\omega})^2}$.

question_latex: Three concentric spherical shells have radii $a, b$ and $c$ $(a < b < c)$ and have surface charge densities $\sigma, -\sigma$ and $\sigma$ respectively. If $V_{A}, V_{B}$ and $V_{C}$ denote the potentials of the three shells, then for $c = a + b$, we have:

Potential at C (radius c): $V_C =  rac{1}{\epsilon_0} ( rac{a^2\sigma}{c} -  rac{b^2\sigma}{c} + c\sigma)$.
Given $c = a + b$.
$V_A =  rac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}(a - b + a + b) =  rac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}(2a)$.
$V_C =  rac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0} ( rac{a^2 - b^2}{c} + c) =  rac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0} ( rac{(a-b)(a+b)}{a+b} + c) =  rac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0} (a - b + c) = V_A$.
$V_B$ is not equal to $V_A$.
So $V_C = V_A 
eq V_B$.

$\vec{E} = -[(-2xy-z^3)\hat{i} + (-x^2)\hat{j} + (-3xz^2)\hat{k}]$.
$\vec{E} = (2xy+z^3)\hat{i} + x^2\hat{j} + 3xz^2\hat{k}$.
subject: Physics

question_latex: The mean free path of electrons in a metal is $4 \times 10^{-8}$ m. The electric field which can give on an average 2 eV energy to an electron in the metal will be in units of V/m:
solution:
Work done $W = F \cdot d = eE \cdot \lambda$.
Given Energy gain = 2 eV = $2e$ Joules (if we keep e as unit) or $2 	imes 1.6 	imes 10^{-19}$ J.
$eE\lambda = 2e$ (in eV) $\implies E\lambda = 2$ (Volts).
$E =  rac{2}{\lambda} =  rac{2}{4 	imes 10^{-8}} = 0.5 	imes 10^8 = 5 	imes 10^7$ V/m.
subject: Physics

question_latex: The ionization energy of the electron in the hydrogen atom in its ground state is 13.6 eV. The atoms are excited to higher energy levels to emit radiations of 6 wavelengths. Maximum wavelength of emitted radiation corresponds to the transition between:
solution:
Number of spectral lines $N =  rac{n(n-1)}{2} = 6$.
$n^2 - n - 12 = 0 \implies (n-4)(n+3) = 0 \implies n=4$.
So the electron is excited to $n=4$.
Radiations are emitted for transitions between 4, 3, 2, 1.
Maximum wavelength corresponds to minimum energy difference $\Delta E$.
Energy levels: $E_n \propto -1/n^2$.
Smallest energy gap among transitions from $n=4$ is $4 	o 3$.
$\Delta E_{4 	o 3}$ is the smallest, so $\lambda$ is max.
subject: Physics

question_latex: Under the influence of a uniform magnetic field, a charged particle moves with constant speed V in a circle of radius R. The time period of rotation of the particle:
options: depends on R and not on V
is independent of both V and R
depends on both V and R
depends on V and not on R
solution: Time period of a charged particle in a magnetic field is $T = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}$.\nIt is independent of velocity $V$ and radius $R$.
subject: Physics

question_latex: The electric field part of an electromagnetic wave in a medium is represented by $E_{y}=2.5 \frac{\text{N}}{\text{C}} \cos[(2\pi \times 10^{6} \frac{\text{rad}}{\text{m}})t - (\pi \times 10^{-2} \frac{\text{rad}}{\text{s}})x]$. The wave is:
options: moving along x direction with frequency $10^{6}$ Hz and wave length 100 m.
moving along x direction with frequency $10^{6}$ Hz and wave length 200 m.
moving along - x direction with frequency $10^{6}$ Hz and wave length 200 m.
moving along y direction with frequency $2\pi \times 10^{6}$ Hz and wave length 200 m.
solution:
Standard equation: $E_y = E_0 \cos(\omega t - kx)$.
Comparing: $\omega = 2\pi 	imes 10^6$.
Frequency $f =  rac{\omega}{2\pi} = 10^6$ Hz.
$k = \pi 	imes 10^{-2}$.
Wavelength $\lambda =  rac{2\pi}{k} =  rac{2\pi}{\pi 	imes 10^{-2}} = 200$ m.
The term $(\omega t - kx)$ indicates propagation in +x direction.
subject: Physics

question_latex: A block of mass M is attached to the lower end of a vertical spring. The spring is hung from a ceiling and has force constant value k. The mass is released from rest with the spring initially unstretched. The maximum extension produced in the length of the spring will be:
solution:
Let max extension be $x$.
Loss in Gravitational PE = Gain in Spring PE.
$Mgx =  rac{1}{2}kx^2$.
$x =  rac{2Mg}{k}$.
subject: Physics

question_latex: Which one of the following is correct pairing of a body part and the kind of muscle tissue that moves it?
options: Biceps of upper arm – Smooth muscle fibres
solution: The iris of the eye contains involuntary smooth muscles (specifically the sphincter pupillae and dilator pupillae) which control the size of the pupil. Biceps are skeletal (striated) muscles. Abdominal wall contains skeletal muscles. Heart wall contains cardiac muscles (involuntary striated).
subject: Biology

question_latex: The epithelial tissue present on the inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes is:
solution: Ciliated epithelium is found in the lining of bronchioles and fallopian tubes. The cilia help in moving particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium (e.g., mucus in bronchioles, ovum in fallopian tubes).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Study the pedigree chart given below: What does it show?

options: Inheritance of a condition like phenylketonuria as an autosomal recessive trait
The pedigree chart is wrong as this is not possible
Inheritance of a recessive sex-linked disease like haemophilia
Inheritance of a sex-linked inborn error of metabolism like phenylketonuria
solution: The pedigree shows unaffected parents having affected children (both male and female). This indicates a recessive trait. Since both sexes are affected, it is likely autosomal. Specifically, the mating of two carriers (heterozygous Aa) can produce affected offspring (aa). Phenylketonuria is an autosomal recessive disorder. It cannot be sex-linked recessive because the father is unaffected, yet the daughter is affected (for a sex-linked recessive trait, an affected daughter must have an affected father).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Manganese is required in:
solution: Manganese serves as a cofactor for the oxygen-evolving complex in photosystem II, playing a crucial role in the photolysis of water (splitting of water) during photosynthesis.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Polyethylene glycol method is used for:
solution: Polyethylene glycol (PEG) is used to induce fusion of protoplasts and can facilitate the uptake of foreign DNA (direct gene transfer) into plant protoplasts without the use of a biological vector.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The floral formula $K_{(5)} C_{(5)} A_{5} G_{(2)}$ is that of:
solution: The formula $K_{(5)} C_{(5)} A_{5} G_{(2)}$ corresponds to the family Solanaceae. Tobacco (*Nicotiana tabacum*) belongs to Solanaceae. Soybean and Sunnhemp are Fabaceae (zygomorphic, $G_1$). Tulip is Liliaceae ($P_{3+3}$).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following groups of animals is bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic?
solution: Aschelminthes are bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic. Sponges are asymmetrical. Coelenterates and Ctenophores are radially symmetrical and diploblastic.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is commonly used in transfer of foreign DNA into crop plants?
solution: *Agrobacterium tumefaciens* contains the Ti plasmid, which acts as a natural vector for delivering DNA into the host plant cells. It is widely used in genetic engineering to create transgenic plants.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following is the correct matching of the events occurring during menstrual cycle?
options: Proliferative phase: Rapid regeneration of myometrium and maturation of Graafian follicle.
Development of corpus luteum: Secretory phase and increased secretion of progesterone.
Menstruation: breakdown of myometrium and ovum not fertilised.
Ovulation: LH and FSH attain peak level and sharp fall in the secretion of progesterone.
solution: The development of the corpus luteum corresponds to the secretory phase (luteal phase), during which there is an increased secretion of progesterone to maintain the endometrium. Option A is incorrect because the endometrium regenerates, not the myometrium. Option C involves breakdown of endometrium. Option D is incorrect because progesterone does not fall sharply at ovulation; it rises after ovulation.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one is the wrong pairing for the disease and its causal organism?
options: Black rust of wheat - Puccinia graminis
Loose smut of wheat - Ustilago nuda
Late blight of potato - Alternaria solani
solution: Late blight of potato is caused by *Phytophthora infestans*. *Alternaria solani* causes early blight of potato.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Global agreement in specific control strategies to reduce the release of ozone depleting substances, was adopted by:
solution: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances that are responsible for ozone depletion.
subject: Biology

question_latex: What is true about Bt toxin?
options: Bt protein exists as active toxin in the Bacillus.
The activated toxin enters the ovaries of the pest to sterilise it and thus prevent its multiplication.
The inactive protoxin gets converted into active form in the insect gut.
solution: Bt toxin exists as inactive protoxin in the bacterium *Bacillus thuringiensis*. When ingested by an insect, the alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilizes the crystals and converts the protoxin into the active toxin.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Peripatus is a connecting link between:
solution: *Peripatus* (Velvet worm) shares characteristics of both Annelida (segmental nephridia, soft body) and Arthropoda (tracheal respiration, claws). Hence, it is a connecting link between them.
subject: Biology

question_latex: T.O. Diener discovered a:
solution: T.O. Diener discovered viroids in 1971. Viroids are infectious agents smaller than viruses, consisting of free low molecular weight RNA without a protein coat.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Seminal plasma in humans is rich in:
options: fructose and calcium but has no enzymes
glucose and certain enzymes but has no calcium
fructose and certain enzymes but poor in calcium
solution: Seminal plasma, secreted by the accessory glands (seminal vesicles, prostate, bulbourethral glands), is rich in fructose, calcium, and certain enzymes.
subject: Biology

question_latex: A fruit developed from hypanthodium inflorescence is called:
solution: A Syconus fruit (e.g., Fig) develops from a hypanthodium inflorescence. Sorosis develops from spike, spadix or catkin (e.g., Pineapple, Jackfruit).
subject: Biology

question_latex: The cell junctions called tight, adhering and gap junctions are found in:
solution: These junctions are characteristic modifications of the plasma membrane in epithelial tissues to provide structural integrity and communication.
subject: Biology

question_latex: What will happen if the stretch receptors of the urinary bladder wall are totally removed?
options: Urine will continue to collect normally in the bladder
Urine will not collect in the bladder
solution: The stretch receptors in the bladder wall detect filling and send signals to the CNS to initiate the micturition reflex. If these are removed, the reflex will not be triggered, and micturition will not occur involuntarily (though overflow incontinence might occur). The solution states 'There will be no micturition' as the reflex is broken.
subject: Biology

question_latex: If a live earthworm is pricked with a needle on its outer surface without damaging its gut, the fluid that comes out is:
solution: The earthworm has a true coelom filled with coelomic fluid which acts as a hydrostatic skeleton. Pricking the body wall releases this milky white alkaline fluid.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The most popularly known blood grouping is the ABO grouping. It is named ABO and not ABC, because 'O' in it refers to having:
options: overdominance of this type on the genes for A and B types
one antibody only either anti-A or anti-B on the RBCS
no antigens A and B on RBCs
other antigens besides A and B on RBCS
solution: Blood group 'O' is characterized by the absence of both Antigen A and Antigen B on the surface of RBCs. The 'O' stands for 'Ohne' (German for without) or Zero/Null.
subject: Biology

question_latex: One of the synthetic auxin is:
solution: NAA (Naphthalene Acetic Acid) and 2,4-D are synthetic auxins. IAA (Indole Acetic Acid) and IBA (Indole Butyric Acid) are generally considered natural auxins found in plants (though IBA can be synthesized).
subject: Biology

question_latex: A person likely to develop tetanus is immunised by administering:
solution: For immediate protection against tetanus (passive immunity), preformed antibodies (Anti-Tetanus Serum or ATS) are administered to neutralize the toxin. The answer key in the document says (3) Weakened germs, with a solution describing 'Tetanus toxoid'. However, in an emergency (person 'likely to develop'), preformed antibodies are used. Tetanus Toxoid (vaccine) is used for active prophylaxis. The provided solution text justifies 'Weakened germs' describing toxoid, but standard medical practice for immediate risk is ATS. The official answer key provided in the source is (3). Note: This question is often debated. In the context of the provided source, it selects (3).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Alzheimer disease in humans is associated with the deficiency of:
solution: Alzheimer's disease is characterized by the degeneration of cholinergic neurons and a significant reduction in the neurotransmitter acetylcholine.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) in a river water:
options: has no relationship with concentration of oxygen in the water.
gives a measure of salmonella in the water.
increases when sewage gets mixed with river water.
remains unchanged when algal bloom occurs.
solution: BOD measures the amount of oxygen required by aerobic microorganisms to decompose organic matter. When sewage (organic waste) mixes with river water, microbial activity increases, leading to a higher BOD.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The genetic defect adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency may be cured permanently by:
options: introducing bone marrow cells producing ADA into cells at early embryonic stages.
periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes having functional ADA cDNA.
solution: Permanent cure for ADA deficiency requires gene therapy at an early embryonic stage, where the functional ADA gene is introduced into bone marrow cells. Treatments like enzyme replacement or lymphocyte infusion are not permanent.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Compared to blood our lymph has:
solution: Lymph is similar to blood plasma but lacks red blood cells (RBCs) and large platelets. It contains more WBCs (lymphocytes) than blood.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Sickle cell anemia is:
options: caused by substitution of valine by glutamic acid in the beta globin chain of haemoglobin
caused by a change in a single base pair of DNA
characterized by elongated sickle like RBCs with a nucleus
solution: Sickle cell anemia is a point mutation (substitution) where Glutamic acid (GAG) is replaced by Valine (GUG) at the 6th position of the beta-globin chain. This is a change in a single base pair (A to U in mRNA, T to A in DNA). Note: Option 1 says Valine by Glutamic acid (reverse). Option 3: RBCs are non-nucleated in mammals. Option 4: It is recessive.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which of the following plant species you would select for the production of bioethanol?
solution: *Jatropha curcas* is a well-known plant for biodiesel/bioethanol production due to its oil-rich seeds.
subject: Biology
topic: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production

question_latex: When breast feeding is replaced by less nutritive food low in proteins and calories; the infants below the age of one year are likely to suffer from:
solution: Marasmus is caused by a simultaneous deficiency of proteins and calories. It typically affects infants under one year of age when mother's milk is replaced too early.
subject: Biology

question_latex: A young infant may be feeding entirely on mother's milk which is white in colour but the stools which the infant passes out is quite yellowish. What is this yellow colour due to?
options: Bile pigments passed through bile juice
solution: The yellow color of stools is primarily due to bile pigments (bilirubin and biliverdin) present in the bile juice secreted by the liver.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following has maximum genetic diversity in India?
solution: India has immense genetic diversity in Rice (50,000 strains) and Mango (1000 varieties). However, among the options provided, Wheat also has high diversity, but typically Rice and Mango are cited. The source key selects Wheat (2). Note: Usually Rice is the top answer in NCERT. If Rice is not an option, Mango or Wheat is selected. Here, the key points to Wheat.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Oxygenic photosynthesis occurs in:
solution: *Oscillatoria* is a cyanobacterium (blue-green algae) and performs oxygenic photosynthesis (evolves oxygen). *Rhodospirillum*, *Chlorobium*, and *Chromatium* are anoxygenic photosynthetic bacteria.
subject: Biology

question_latex: There is no DNA in:
solution: Mature mammalian Red Blood Cells (RBCs) lack a nucleus and other organelles like mitochondria, so they do not contain DNA.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Given below is a schematic break-up of the phases / stages of cell cycle: Which one of the following is the correct indication of the stage/phase in the cell cycle?

subject: Biology

question_latex: Tiger is not a resident in which one of the following national park?
solution: Gir National Park is famous for the Asiatic Lion (*Panthera leo persica*). Tigers are not found there. Sunderbans, Jim Corbett, and Ranthambhore are famous Tiger reserves.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following statements is true regarding digestion and absorption of food in humans?
options: Fructose and amino acids are absorbed through intestinal mucosa with the help of carrier ions like $Na^{+}$
Chylomicrons are small lipoprotein particles that are transported from intestine into blood capillaries.
About 60% of starch is hydrolysed by salivary amylase in our mouth.
Oxyntic cells in our stomach secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen.
solution: Absorption of substances like fructose and some amino acids involves facilitated transport with carrier ions like $Na^+$. Chylomicrons enter lacteals (lymph), not blood capillaries directly. Only 30% of starch is hydrolyzed in the mouth. Oxyntic cells secrete HCl; peptic/chief cells secrete pepsinogen.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Synapsis occurs between:
options: a male and a female gamete
solution: Synapsis is the pairing of two homologous chromosomes that occurs during the prophase I (specifically Zygotene stage) of meiosis.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Given below is a diagrammatic sketch of a portion of human male reproductive system. Select the correct set of the names of the parts labelled A, B, C, D.
question_svg: <svg width='300' height='300' viewBox='0 0 300 300' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M100,50 L100,150' stroke='black' fill='none'/><text x='80' y='50'>A</text><ellipse cx='120' cy='150' rx='20' ry='10' stroke='black' fill='none'/><text x='150' y='150'>B</text><rect x='100' y='170' width='40' height='20' stroke='black' fill='none'/><text x='150' y='180'>C</text><circle cx='120' cy='200' r='5' stroke='black' fill='none'/><text x='150' y='200'>D</text></svg>
options: A-vas deferens, B-seminal vesicle, C-prostate, D-bulbourethral gland
A-vas deferens, B-seminal vesicle, C-bulbourethral gland, D-prostate
A-ureter, B-seminal vesicle, C-prostate, D-bulbourethral gland
A-ureter, B-prostate, C-seminal vesicle, D-bulbourethral gland
solution: Based on the standard anatomy of the male reproductive system: A is Vas Deferens (carrying sperm), B is Seminal Vesicle (paired glands), C is Prostate (single gland), D is Bulbourethral gland (Cowper's gland, paired, below prostate).
subject: Biology

question_latex: What is not true for genetic code?
options: A codon in mRNA is read in a non-contiguous fashion
solution: The genetic code is read in a contiguous fashion, meaning there are no punctuations (commas) between codons. 'Non-contiguous' is false. It is universal, degenerate, and unambiguous.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following plants is monoecious?
solution: *Pinus* is monoecious (male and female cones on the same tree). *Cycas*, *Papaya*, and *Marchantia* are typically dioecious (separate male and female plants).
subject: Biology

question_latex: Cyclic photophosphorylation results in the formation of:
solution: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves only Photosystem I and results in the synthesis of ATP only. It does not produce NADPH or oxygen.
subject: Biology

question_latex: The letter T in T-lymphocyte refers to:
solution: T-lymphocytes mature in the **Thymus** gland.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Foetal ejection reflex in human female is induced by:
solution: The foetal ejection reflex (parturition) is initiated by signals from the fully developed foetus and the placenta, which induce mild uterine contractions (fetal ejection reflex). This triggers the release of oxytocin.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Anatomically fairly old dicotyledonous root is distinguished from the dicotyledonous stem by
solution: In roots, the protoxylem is exarch (towards periphery). In stems, the protoxylem is endarch (towards center). This position distinguishes them.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Plasmodesmata are:
options: Membranes connecting the nucleus with plasmalemma
solution: Plasmodesmata are cytoplasmic bridges (connections) between adjacent plant cells that traverse the cell walls, allowing communication and transport.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Removal of introns and joining the exons in a defined order in a transcription unit is called:
solution: Splicing is the process in eukaryotic mRNA processing where non-coding introns are removed and coding exons are joined together.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Phylogenetic system of classification is based on:
solution: Phylogenetic classification systems are based on evolutionary relationships between organisms.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which part of human brain is concerned with the regulation of body temperature?
solution: The hypothalamus contains the thermostat of the body and regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst, etc.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Semiconservative replication of DNA was first demonstrated in:
solution: Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl demonstrated the semiconservative nature of DNA replication in 1958 using *Escherichia coli* and heavy nitrogen isotopes.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which one of the following pairs of animals comprises 'jawless fishes'?
solution: Jawless fishes belong to the class Cyclostomata. Examples include Lampreys (*Petromyzon*) and Hagfishes (*Myxine*). Eels, Rohu, etc., are jawed fishes.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Which of the following is a pair of viral diseases?
solution: Common Cold is caused by Rhinovirus and AIDS is caused by HIV. Both are viral diseases. Dysentery is bacterial/amoebic, Typhoid and Tuberculosis are bacterial, Ringworm is fungal.
subject: Biology

question_latex: Aerobic respiratory pathway is appropriately termed:
solution: The respiratory pathway is involved in both breakdown (catabolism) of substrates and synthesis (anabolism) of biomolecules (e.g., Acetyl CoA is used for fatty acid synthesis). Hence, it is termed an amphibolic pathway.
subject: Biology

question_latex: A country with a high rate of population growth took measures to reduce it. The Figure below shows age-sex pyramids of populations A and B twenty years apart. Select the correct interpretation about them:
question_svg: <svg width='400' height='200' viewBox='0 0 400 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='100' y='20' font-weight='bold'>A</text><text x='300' y='20' font-weight='bold'>B</text><path d='M50,180 L150,180 L100,30 Z' fill='none' stroke='black'/><text x='100' y='190'>Broad Base</text><path d='M270,180 L330,180 L330,100 L300,30 L270,100 Z' fill='none' stroke='black'/><text x='300' y='190'>Narrower Base</text></svg>

'B' is more recent showing that population is very young.
'A' is the earlier pyramid and no change has occurred in the growth rate.
